Pharmacists submit 6-point proposal to reform commission
2025-02-19T20:33:43+06:00 | Star Digital Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/pharmacists-submit-6-point-proposal-reform-commission-3828536

The Bangladesh Pharmacists Forum has submitted a six-point proposal to the Health Sector Reform Commission, aiming to improve healthcare services to international standards.

Their demands include recruiting graduate pharmacists in hospitals and reserving top positions at the Essential Drugs Company Limited and the Directorate General of Drug Administration (DGDA) for pharmacists.

The forum submitted the proposals to the commission's office, its president, Azibur Rahman, told The Daily Star today.

In its proposal, the organisation noted that in developed countries, pharmacists work alongside doctors and nurses in hospitals.

However, despite pharmacy education beginning in Bangladesh in 1965, no pharmacists have been recruited in hospitals.

As a result, patients often face issues like improper use of medicines, it stated, stressing the need for graduate pharmacists in hospitals.

The organisation also pointed out that the government has appointed a prominent pharmacist as the managing director of the state-run Essential Drugs Company Limited.

It demanded that this position, along with the post of DGDA director general, be reserved for pharmacists.

Other proposals included appointing at least two pharmacists at district-level drug administration offices and ensuring the inclusion of a pharmacist in the reform commission and all relevant health ministry committees.
